subject: Privacy terms: template provision + subprocessor & signing options
messages:
From: Ankur Patel <ankur.patel@fintech.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintech.co>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Privacy terms & DPA - initial ask

Hi Jordan,

We chatted with Ben last week and the team asked me to kick off privacy/contracting for the integration. Can you send our legal the standard DPA and a current list of subprocessors? Procurement also needs to know signing options (DocuSign vs AdobeSign) and whether Redwood supports an audit/attestation packet (SOC 2 + controls). We also need a quick confirmation on data residency (US-only vs transfers) and preferred routing for EU customers.

Attached: FinTech_Security_Questionnaire.docx (answers TBD).

Can you provide a DPA template and an expected timeline for review/signature? Prefer to keep this tight — we'd like the DPA in place before the pilot starts mid-March.

Thanks,
Ankur Patel
Head of Integrations 
FinTech Co
ankur.patel@fintech.co
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ankur Patel <ankur.patel@fintech.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Privacy terms & DPA - initial ask

Hi Ankur — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Laura (legal) and Priyom (privacy) so we can move quickly.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provide our current standard DPA and an exported subprocessor list.
- We typically execute via DocuSign; AdobeSign is supported but procurement-driven exceptions happen.
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II and can share the attestation under an NDA; we can also provide a redacted controls matrix.
- Default hosting is US regions, but we support EU routing for customer accounts (we'd confirm exact egress/dataflows for your pilot).

Attached: Redwood_Standard_DPA_v1.2.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2027-02.xlsx (live snapshot).

Laura — can you confirm if we can offer a short Data Annex for FinTech to lock residency? Also, if FinTech wants specific transfer mechanisms (SCCs), we should note that in the DPA.

Proposed next steps:
1) FinTech provides completed questionnaire + ideal signature party.
2) Redwood legal provides tracked redlines (if any) within 2 business days.
3) Quick 30-min call for any substantive redline walkthrough — Ben/Marcus to join for product/dataflow questions.

Jordan Blake
Senior Partnerships 
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ankur Patel <ankur.patel@fintech.co>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Privacy terms & DPA - initial ask

Ankur / Jordan — thanks. I reviewed the template and put an initial set of comments together. High-level items:

1) Subprocessors & notices: We'll provide the current list (attached). We accept a periodic push-notification model for subprocessor updates; if FinTech requires prior approval for specific classes of subprocessors, we'll need to scope that in the Data Annex.

2) International transfers: Redwood can support EU account routing and is open to executing SCCs where required. If FinTech needs data to remain in EU physical locations for the pilot, we'll add a residency clause in the Annex.

3) Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA. We can also provide a redacted controls matrix and details on key technical measures (encryption in transit/at rest, access controls).

4) Signing: DocuSign is our default. Procurement sometimes requests AdobeSign — we can accommodate, but certain templates have DocuSign-only audit trails; if procurement prefers AdobeSign, please advise and note whether that preference is contractual.

5) Liability/limits/redlines: I flagged a few standard career-capped clauses (liability cap, warranty language) and suggested language for breach notification timelines. I'll share a tracked PDF shortly.

Attached: Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2027-02.xlsx, Redwood_DPA_Redlines_2027-02-11.pdf

If you prefer a short call to walk through the redlines, I'm free tomorrow 11:00–12:00 PST.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: Ankur Patel <ankur.patel@fintech.co>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintech.co>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Privacy terms & DPA - initial ask

Laura — thanks for the fast review. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement prefers DocuSign but will accept AdobeSign if there's a technical reason. DocuSign is our standard for onboarding.
- We'll sign SCCs if needed; for the pilot we'd prefer the EU-routing Data Annex rather than moving production data.
- SOC 2 under NDA is fine — I'll share the PO-approved NDA via procurement.

I've attached our proposed redlines to the DPA (high level: clarifications on liability carveouts, regulatory cooperation clause, and data retention specifics). If you can review the PDF and confirm which items are non-starters, that would be great.

Also propose a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:30 PST to go over redlines + dataflow (Marcus please join to confirm KV-cache/e2e flow for pilot).

Attached: FinTech_DPA_Redlines_2027-02-11.pdf

Thanks,
Ankur Patel
Head of Integrations

Ankur — appreciate the quick turnaround. Laura and Priyom reviewed FinTech's redlines and marked a handful as discussable vs. non-starters (see Redwood_DPA_Redlines_2027-02-12.pdf in the drive link below).

To keep momentum: we've uploaded an executable DPA envelope via DocuSign for the items where we already have alignment (SCCs, subprocessor notification cadence, SOC 2 NDA). Please review the envelope and sign if acceptable: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-redwood-dpa

If there are still open legal items after FinTech signs, we'll treat those as a short amendment and schedule a follow-up call. Marcus will coordinate a 30-min technical session on Monday to confirm routing and KV-cache behavior for the pilot.

Next steps:
- Ankur/procurement: review & sign DocuSign envelope (link above).
- If signed, legal will finalize the Data Annex and return a countersigned copy within 2 business days.
- Marcus/Ben/Jordan: schedule technical alignment meeting for Monday 10:30 PST.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.
